name: Vṛndāvana
about:
Akbar visited Vṛndāvana in 1573 and met Jīva Gosvāmī; it is said he was taken blindfolded to Nidhuvana and understood that Vṛndāvana is the great dhāma. With his leave the Hindu rājās of his court built temples: about 1570 the temple of Madana-mohana; then Rāya Siṁha of Bikaner the temple of Gopīnātha; Mānasiṁha of Ambara (1590) the temple of Govindajī; and the Chauhan Rāja Lonakaraṇa (1627) that of Nanda-kiśora. Akbar forbade the killing of animals in Vraja-maṇḍala.
Kuṇḍas: Lalitā-kuṇḍa (SW of Nikuñjavana), Viśākhā-kuṇḍa (in Nidhuvana), Brahma-kuṇḍa (NW of the Govinda temple), Gajarāja-kuṇḍa (in the Raṅganāthajī temple) and Govinda-kuṇḍa (east of Vṛndāvana; some say Govindajī appeared there).
Famous deities: (1) Rādhā-Govinda, revealed by Rūpa Gosvāmī — now in Jaipur; (2) Gopīnātha, revealed by Madhu Paṇḍita — now in Jaipur; (3) Madana-mohana, served by Sanātana Gosvāmī — now in Karauli; (4) Rādhā-ramaṇa, revealed by Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī; (5) Rādhā-vinoda, revealed by Lokanātha Gosvāmī — now in Jaipur; (6) Rādhā-Mādhava, served by Jayadeva — now at Jaipur Ghāṭī; (7) Rādhā-Dāmodara, served by Jīva Gosvāmī — now in Jaipur; (8) Rādhā-vallabha, revealed by Harivaṁśa Gosvāmī; (9) Baṅkebihārī, revealed by Haridāsa Svāmī; (10) Śyāmasundara, served by Śyāmānanda Prabhu; (11) Gokulānanda, served by Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura; (12) Nityānanda-Gaurāṅga served by Murāri Gupta, before the Vanakhaṇḍī Mahādeva (the name Murāri Gupta is carved at its feet; it was found in the earth in Bīrbhūm and served at Siuḍi before coming to Vṛndāvana).
Famous samādhis: see the places of each temple, Dhīra-samīra, Kāliya-daha and Keśī-ghāṭa; there are many more in the Samāja-bāṭī of the sixty-four mahāntas.

name: Govindajī temple
aka: Govindaji, Govinda temple, Rādhā-Govinda mandira, Govindadeva
about:
Temple of Śrī Rādhā-Govinda, the deity revealed by Rūpa Gosvāmī (now in Jaipur); built by Mānasiṁha of Ambara in 1590. North-west of it is the Brahma-kuṇḍa.
North-east of the Govinda temple, in the Samāja-bāṭī of the sixty-four mahāntas, is the samādhi of Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī; many other samādhis are there.

name: Madana-mohana temple
aka: Madanamohana, Madan Mohan, Dvādaśāditya-ṭilā, Dvadasaditya tila
about: Temple of Śrī Madana-mohana, served by Sanātana Gosvāmī (the deity is now in Karauli); built about 1570. The samādhi of Sanātana Gosvāmī is below the Dvādaśāditya-ṭilā.

name: Rādhā-Dāmodara temple
about: Temple of Śrī Rādhā-Dāmodara, served by Jīva Gosvāmī (the deity is now in Jaipur). The samādhis of Rūpa Gosvāmī and of Jīva Gosvāmī are in this temple.

name: Rādhā-ramaṇa temple
about: Temple of Śrī Rādhā-ramaṇa, revealed by Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī. His samādhi is beside the temple.

name: Gokulānanda temple
about: Temple of Śrī Gokulānanda, served by Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura. The samādhis of Lokanātha Gosvāmī and of Narottama Ṭhākura are here. (Lokanātha's Rādhā-vinoda is now in Jaipur.)

name: Gopīnātha temple
about: Temple of Śrī Gopīnātha, the deity revealed by Madhu Paṇḍita (now in Jaipur); built by Rāya Siṁha of Bikaner. Madhu Paṇḍita's samādhi is beside the temple.

name: Śyāmasundara temple
about: Temple of Śrī Śyāmasundara, served by Śyāmānanda Prabhu; his samādhi is in the temple.

name: Dhīra-samīra
about: The samādhis of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya, of Rāmacandra Kavirāja and of Gaurīdāsa Paṇḍita are at Dhīra-samīra.

name: Kāliya-daha
about: The samādhi of Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī is at Kāliya-daha.

name: Keśī-ghāṭa
about: The danta-samādhi of Gadādhara Paṇḍita Gosvāmī: while he was still present, one of his broken teeth was taken to Vṛndāvana by his nephew Nayanānanda Prabhu, who buried it and gave it samādhi; since then it is called the «Danta-samāja».

name: Rādhā-kuṇḍa
aka: Radhakund, Radha-kund, Radha kunda, Śyāma-kuṇḍa, Syamakunda, Shyam kund
about:
The crown jewel of Vraja, where Kṛṣṇa killed Ariṣṭāsura; the great tīrtha of the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas (see the Vṛndāvana-līlāmṛta). All the temples of Vṛndāvana are found here too. After killing the bull-demon Kṛṣṇa called all the tīrthas and manifested Śyāma-kuṇḍa; Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī then made a kuṇḍa of her own, west of it, where Ariṣṭa's hoof had struck, the sakhīs digging the earth with their hands.
Ghāṭs: Govinda-ghāṭa (where Sanātana Gosvāmī saw the serpent-like braids on the backs of the gopīs), Mānasapāvana-ghāṭa, Pañcapāṇḍava-ghāṭa, Rādhāvallabha-ghāṭa, the sitting place of Mahāprabhu, Madana-mohana-ghāṭa, Saṅgama-ghāṭa, the Jhūlana ghāṭa, Jāhnavā's ghāṭa, Gayā-ghāṭa.
Samādhis: the citā-samādhi of Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī together with those of other Gosvāmīs (the names are not legible in the OCR); the puṣpa-samādhi of Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī on the north bank; south of the kuṇḍa the samādhi of Rājendra Gosvāmī.
Rādhā-kuṇḍa appeared at midnight on Kārtika kṛṣṇa aṣṭamī: hundreds of thousands bathe then; many pilgrims also come at the Gauḍīya pūrṇimā, in Puruṣottama month and for the niyama-sevā.

name: Govardhana
aka: Govardhan, Govardhana-giri, Girirāja, Giriraj, Govinda-kuṇḍa, Anyor
about:
Śrī Girirāja, the place of many pastimes of Kṛṣṇa; the arcā-pīṭha of Śrī Harideva.
Govinda-kuṇḍa, at the foot of Girirāja, where Kṛṣṇa was bathed as Govinda: on its east bank the Govinda temple; on its south bank the temple of Śrīnāthajī and the sitting place of Mādhavendra Purī. Here Gopāla, as a boy of Vraja, brought milk to Mādhavendra Purī, then told him in a dream who he was and was brought out of the bower. West of the kuṇḍa is a Govardhana śilā with the marks of a hand and a stick.
